context-window: Illustrate a horizontal glass "window" or frame stretching across the image, subdivided into a long sequence of small uniform tiles (tokens), with the leftmost tiles depicting the start of a project — architectural blueprints or foundational code — and the tiles progressing rightward through a timeline of related material: snippets of code, chat bubbles, a research paper's pages, project notes — all visibly present and connected within the frame. On one side, label the frame's total span "1,000,000 tokens ≈ hundreds of thousands of words" to show scale. Inside the frame, at a point near the right edge, place a small AI model icon (a simple chip or head silhouette) with faint dotted lines reaching backward to a few of the earliest tiles, showing it "seeing" and referencing that early material while working on the newest tile. To convey the caveat, show a couple of tiles far in the past rendered slightly faded or blurred, with one dotted line breaking before it reaches them — indicating that even within a large window, some earlier information can be lost or handled unreliably.
mixture-of-experts: Illustration: a wide horizontal diagram of a single glowing token entering from the left and passing through a routing gate depicted as a small funnel or switchboard with a spotlight beam; behind the gate, arrange a large grid of 896 uniform small server-rack or node icons labeled "experts," most rendered in dim grey (idle), with only 16 of them lit up in bright color and connected by highlighted lines showing the token's path through them to an output arrow on the right; include a small caption-style annotation contrasting "Total parameters: 896 experts (huge)" near the full grid with "Active per token: 16 experts (small)" near the lit ones, visually reinforcing that only a fraction of the model's capacity is engaged for any single computation.
model-distillation: Illustration: a large, ornate "parent" robot or server tower labeled with a generic tag like "Model A," seated at a desk, with a stream of glowing question-and-answer bubbles flowing from its head into a funnel. The funnel feeds down into a smaller, sleeker "child" robot labeled "Model B," which is visibly growing or sharpening as it absorbs the stream. Behind the parent robot, a faint, semi-transparent cloud of tiny document, image, and code icons flows upward into its own head, echoing the same funnel-and-stream visual so viewers can see the parallel: the parent was itself built by drawing freely on scattered human-made material, while it now objects to the child drawing on its own output. A dotted line or broken chain between the two robots, with a small "Terms of Service" document icon and a "?" mark hovering near it, signals the unresolved legal and ethical dispute, while a faint scale in the background, tipped unevenly, underscores the accusation of double standards.
open-weight-model: Illustration: a split-panel diagram contrasting two AI distribution models side by side. On the left, labeled "CLOSED MODEL," a padlocked corporate server tower sits behind a wall, with a thin one-way pipe labeled "API access (pay-per-use)" extending outward to small user icons, and a red kill-switch cable connecting the server to the company — illustrating that access can be revoked or shut off remotely. On the right, labeled "OPEN-WEIGHT MODEL," a block of numerical values labeled "trained weights" flows downward through an open download arrow into many independent computers, workbenches, and hands — some fine-tuning it, some stripping away a small "safety guardrail" icon shown breaking off — with no cable connecting back to the original company, emphasizing that once released, the weights are irreversible and permanently out of the original publisher's control. A small dashed box near the open side notes "training data & code: usually NOT included," distinguishing this from full open-source software. Below both panels, a balance scale labels the two consequences: "Competitive pressure on closed providers" versus "Harder safety & misuse questions."
